name: Tool Proficiency (General)
description: General proficiency with the tools and infrastructure common to security lab work. Covers Linux command line, scripting (Python, Bash), version control (git), virtualization and lab environments, and the ability to learn and evaluate new tools effectively.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to security lab tooling or Linux environments

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Basic familiarity with Linux CLI and lab environment concepts
evidence: Can navigate a Linux filesystem and use basic commands
Understands the purpose of virtual machines and lab isolation

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Uses standard lab tools and environments with guidance
evidence: Can set up and use lab VMs for testing
Writes basic scripts (Bash or Python) to automate tasks
Uses git for version control at a basic level
Can install and configure common security tools

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently manages tools, environments, and automation for engagements
evidence: Builds and maintains lab environments for specific engagements
Writes functional automation scripts without guidance
Evaluates and adopts new tools independently
Comfortable with networking, containers, and infrastructure tooling

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Develops custom tooling; maintains lab infrastructure; mentors on tool usage
evidence: Develops and maintains custom tools used by the team
Manages shared lab infrastructure and environments
Mentors junior staff on tooling and environment setup

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Architects lab infrastructure; develops frameworks; trains teams
evidence: Designed or architects the lab's technical infrastructure
Develops tool frameworks used across the team
Trains teams on tooling best practices and infrastructure

assessment_methods.description: Set up a lab environment for a specified engagement type from scratch
Review scripts and automation created by the individual
